V88 · 14:55–15:00 refinement

Implemented, with visual gaps remaining. The original remains the benchmark. Equal complete viewports replace the cropped screenshots. The standing coach was present in full V87 frames; the screenshot crop hid it.

Original · unchanged referenceV88 · editable reconstruction

Each step is exactly 1/30 second of source footage. This contact review uses 480×270 JPEG thumbnails; the comparison video contains 960×540 panels. 0.05× displays 1.5 source frames per real second.

What changed

A connected manifold mannequin replaces the visible primitive assembly. Each actor has 51 joints, including finger chains, and four normalized skin weights per vertex. The active mesh has 18,280 vertices and 36,556 triangles. A separate higher-resolution candidate is retained. Torso weights exclude unrelated limb influence. The scene has a thin illuminated tabletop, black front, curved chair rails, brimmed cylindrical hat, directional shading and animated background smoke. Final temporal review restored the outgoing near-camera coach passage and the blue figure’s rear-to-profile crossing from right to left. The unmatched held shoe is omitted from the refined view and preserved in V87.

Measured and checked

Each shot contains both actors; foreground occlusion and frame cropping can hide part or all of one actor. The crimson-to-blue cut remains at frame116, source898.866667. The table's authored front edge is horizontal, compared with roughly15° slope in V87. Limits and refinement backlog

This is a foundation correction, not a certified match. Exact silhouette overlap ≥0.90 has not been measured. One sampled head estimate exceeds the proposed2% diagonal threshold. Body proportions, hand shapes/contact, seated depth trajectory and coach motion still differ. The blue camera fit has17–31px RMS residual against approximate manual landmarks. Smoke remains an authored2D effect rather than reconstructed volumetric simulation. Lighting lacks true cast shadows. The new body starts at895, so the incoming primitive-to-skinned-model join remains visible. Refining that preceding shot is the next priority before extending coverage.

All150 source frames were decoded and deterministic outputs rendered. Staged frames and the encoded comparison were inspected as stills. Continuous audiovisual playback, continuous0.05× viewing, live browser performance and Godot import were not verified. A real100-second0.05× comparison is supplied for review; producing it is not a claim to have watched it continuously.

Editable delivery

The native editor retains MotionCore timing and per-instance controls. Open the14:55–15:00 section and edit the JSON settings. World roots, camera eye/target/focal, torso flexion and light strength are explicit. Joint offsets and source-time joint keys are supported, including fingers. Object visibility and Canvas transforms remain available. Set checkpointRefinementEnabled:false to restore the preserved V87 renderer.

The two standard glTF2 scenes include skinned actors, independent skeletons, hat parts, camera motion and animation. Native varying focal/FOV keys are retained in glTF extras; core glTF camera imports use the first-frame FOV unless the importing engine applies those keys. The crimson scene also contains the table/chair geometry. Skin deformation was numerically compared with the CPU renderer at three sampled poses per scene. Native smoke/shading remain in editable project code; imported glTF materials may render differently. glTF files are split by shot to preserve visibility and cut semantics without pretending a cross-shot body turn.

No remote commit or deployment was made. Work stops at source15:00. Original media is only used in diagnostic comparisons, never as a substitute texture in the reconstruction.
